title: Hook (0:00–0:06)
text: [sarcastic] Okay. [short pause] Let's back up. [pause] Ten hours earlier.

title: Premise (0:06–0:18)
text: [warmly] What if you woke up in a world where zombies only come out at night… [short pause] and you had exactly ten hours, with nothing but your bare hands, [short pause] to build a home they can't get into?

title: The rules (0:18–0:30)
text: Rule one: the sun keeps time. [short pause] Rule two: everything you need is somewhere in this meadow. [short pause] Rule three: [slowly] when the sun touches the horizon… [short pause] they come. [happy] Let's see what you can build.

title: No tools (0:30–0:50)
text: [mischievously] First problem: you can't build anything without tools. You look around. Trees, grass, rocks, more grass. So you grab the best tool in the whole meadow, a nice sturdy stick, and give that tree everything you've got. [pause] [sarcastic] And now your only tool is… [short pause] was… [short pause] a stick.

title: The rock hits back (0:50–1:10)
text: So you do what every survivor in history has done. You hit a rock with a rock. [short pause] [laughs] The rock… hits back. Your teeth are still buzzing. But on the fourth try it splits, and suddenly you're holding a sharp edge. Tie it to a branch with some vine, and [excited] congratulations: you've invented the axe.

title: Gear (1:10–1:35)
text: [excited] With an axe, a tree takes minutes, not hours. One tree, two trees, five. Every log is a wall, a beam, a spike for later. And while you're at it, a wooden shield. Is it good? [short pause] No. [short pause] Is it better than nothing? [short pause] Absolutely. Two hours down, and you've got gear.

title: Picking the spot (1:35–2:00)
text: [curious] Here's what nobody tells you: where you build matters more than what you build. Tall grass hides them until they're on top of you. Open fields mean they come from every direction. But a little hill with giant boulders at your back? They can only come from one side, and from up here, you'll see them coming.

title: The build (2:00–2:35)
text: [excited] Foundation first, made of stone, so nothing digs underneath. Then the frame: four corner posts, buried deep. Then the walls, log by log, gaps packed with mud. Then a proper roof, because if every zombie movie has taught you anything, it's never sleep somewhere they can drop in. [softly] Four hours in, and for the first time, you have somewhere that's yours.

title: The crystal (2:35–3:15)
text: You need more stone, so you start chipping at the boulders. [softly] [curious] And that's when you find it. A crack, and something glowing inside. A crystal that shines on its own. In a world where the monsters come out in the dark, a light that never runs out isn't treasure. [short pause] It's a weapon. [happy] Lash a shard to a long pole: crystal spear. Strap leather and scrap metal to your arms and legs: armour. It's ugly. It squeaks. [warmly] You love it.

title: The mistake (3:15–3:50)
text: [happy] Seven hours gone. You've got a house, a spear and armour. Honestly? You're feeling pretty good. You even have time to sit down. [dramatically] But look around. A house isn't a fortress. There's nothing between those walls and the open meadow. And when the sun goes down, you're going to find out about the one thing you got wrong.

title: Spikes and trench (3:50–4:20)
text: [dramatically] Step one of turning a house into a fortress: make it hurt to touch. You sharpen every log you have left and hammer them in a ring around the cabin, every single point facing out. Anything that wants in has to go through them. Then a trench, outside the spikes. It won't stop them, but it slows them down. And slow zombies are zombies you can count.

title: The vine rope (4:20–4:34)
text: You still need a way in and out, so: a drawbridge over the trench, held up with rope. [short pause] Well. Vine rope. [short pause] You give it a tug. It'll hold. [pause] [sarcastic] …Probably.

title: Lookout and the boulder (4:34–5:00)
text: Up on the roof: a lookout, and arrows tipped with that glowing crystal. Every shot is a flare, and every flare shows you where they are. And one last thing: a boulder hanging over your front door, for when every other plan fails. You really hope you never need it. [pause] [softly] Then the sun touches the horizon.

title: Eyes in the dark (5:00–5:25)
text: [whispers] The music stops. Even the bugs go quiet. You hold your breath and listen. [pause] Nothing. [pause] [whispers] Then one pair of eyes. [short pause] Then ten. [short pause] Then you stop counting. [nervous] They don't run. They don't need to. They know you're not going anywhere.

title: First wave (5:25–5:55)
text: [nervous] The first ones hit the trench and tumble in. The ones behind climb right over them, straight into the spikes. And every crystal arrow lights up the dark for a heartbeat, so you know exactly where they are. One. [short pause] Two. [short pause] Five. [happy] The walls are holding. Everything you built today is working.

title: The ground shakes (5:55–6:10)
text: [softly] Then, just like that, they pull back. For a moment, you actually think you've won. [pause] [cautiously] And then the pebbles on the roof start to bounce. [short pause] The ground is shaking.

title: The Brute (6:10–6:35)
text: [nervous] Something big is coming. It doesn't stop at the trench. It doesn't care about the spikes. It goes straight for the gate. And the drawbridge rope… [short pause] [sighs] the vine rope. [short pause] Of course. [short pause] It was always going to be the vine rope.

title: Close combat (6:35–7:05)
text: [excited] They're inside. No more arrows. Spear out. You jump down, off the wall, duck, spin, back to the doorway, because if they get through that door, it's over. One of them lands a hit, and that armour you almost didn't bother making? [breathless] It just saved your life.

title: Last resort (7:05–7:20)
text: [breathless] But there are too many. Back up the ladder, onto the roof. Nowhere left to run. [slowly] The big one is right below you, at the front door. [short pause] Just one rope… [short pause] and one boulder.

title: Sunrise (7:20–7:35)
text: [mischievously] Goodbye, big guy. [long pause] [excited] And right on cue… [short pause] sunrise. Every one of them the light touches crumbles into ash.

title: Outro (7:35–8:00)
text: [tired] You made it. One night. The gate is gone, your spear is chipped, and you can't feel your arms. [dramatically] But the sun is already moving again, and tonight, they'll come back bigger. [pause] [warmly] So, what would you build first? Tell me in the comments. And if you want to see night two… you know what to do.
